thread:
maya_sec: Heads up — at ~2026-03-23T02:12:03Z we saw a ~2.1k spike in TLS handshake rejects from eu-west ingress -> svc-auth. Seems correlated with last-night RBAC change. Client certs failing CN check

rotator-bot: rotator: completed rotation job keystore-eu-20260323-01 at 2026-03-23T01:58:00Z (job id: 9f3a). No errors reported during rotation.

oscar_sre: Can you paste a sample error line? Also check KMS unwrap/audit for who decrypted the key. Could be the rotator used the wrong principal.

maya_sec: snippet from ingress logs: 
```
2026-03-23T02:11:58Z ingress-1 svc-auth="svc-auth-01" tls: handshake error: remote error: tls: bad certificate (client CN=svc-auth-old, expected svc-auth)
2026-03-23T02:12:01Z ingress-2 svc-auth="svc-auth-02" tls: handshake error: remote error: tls: bad certificate (client CN=svc-auth-old, expected svc-auth)
```

liam_dev: We merged RBAC PR #3247 yesterday to consolidate secret access under group platform-deploy. That PR changed binding ownership for secret/keystore-eu from service-account:svc-auth to group:platform-deploy. Might explain why the rotator picked up the old identity? PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/infra/pulls/3247

nina_devex: Quick checklist: 1) audit KMS decrypt logs, 2) confirm which service account the rotator used, 3) check keystore annotations in k8s, 4) if mismatched, regrant and re-run rotation in canary.

oscar_sre: I pulled KMS audit log for the key; time range 01:55-02:05Z shows decrypts by principal "svc-auth-old@infra.redwood" (3 calls) and by "rotator-sa@infra.redwood" (1 call). That's odd — expected only rotator-sa. Audit excerpt:
```
{"timestamp":"2026-03-23T01:57:59Z","principal":"svc-auth-old@infra.redwood","action":"Decrypt","resource":"projects/.../keyRings/keystore-eu/cryptoKeys/keystore-key"}
{"timestamp":"2026-03-23T01:58:01Z","principal":"rotator-sa@infra.redwood","action":"Decrypt","resource":".../keystore-key"}
```

maya_sec: So looks like svc-auth-old still has key access. That explains old CN in certs. How did svc-auth-old get access after the RBAC change?

liam_dev: The RBAC change removed service-account binding but left a legacy IAM binding at the project-level (automated scripts didn't remove). I can see an override in terraform state: `iam_binding.project.legacy_keystore_binding` not removed.

nina_devex: Action plan: (A) remove legacy binding for svc-auth-old from KMS; (B) rotate keystore in canary with rotator-sa; (C) deploy a short-lived regression test that does s_client -> verify CNs; (D) create audit alert for KMS decrypts by non-rotator principals. Who owns A/B/C?

oscar_sre: I can do A now (will remove binding). Will notify when done.

rotator-bot: rotator: starting rotation job keystore-eu-20260323-02 (canary) using rotator-sa@infra.redwood

oscar_sre: Binding removed @2026-03-23T02:18:45Z. Verified no remaining svc-auth-old principals in IAM policy.

liam_dev: Re-run rotator canary now?

rotator-bot: rotator: canary rotation completed at 2026-03-23T02:20:30Z. Issued new certs with CN=svc-auth.

maya_sec: Quick connectivity test from eu-west egress: `openssl s_client -connect svc-auth.euw.internal:443 -tlsextdebug -status` shows cert CN=svc-auth and handshake succeeding.

oscar_sre: Ingress handshake rejects dropped to baseline after 02:21Z. Monitoring graph: connection_fail_rate metric back to normal.

nina_devex: Follow-ups: 1) Liam to remove legacy terraform state entry and submit PR to reconcile infra, 2) Sec to add KMS-decrypt alert rule (any decrypt by non-rotator-sa for keystore keys), 3) Run a one-week audit report and include in next week's security sync.

liam_dev: Will open PR to remove legacy binding and include test that verifies keystore IAM parity. Targeting PR today.

maya_sec: Also adding incident note to security tracker (P2) with root cause = leftover IAM binding after RBAC consolidation, contributing factor = no alerting for unexpected KMS-decrypt principals.

oscar_sre: Good catch — thanks team. If anyone sees related spikes in other regions, ping and we'll triage similarly. :thumbsup:

nina_devex: I'll own the postmortem write-up template and make sure we document the mitigation steps and alerting rule.
